lessons.title: Callable declarations and first-class callables
lessons.summary: If the callable is plusOne(...) instead, what prints?
explanation: A callable parameter accepts an invocable value, such as a Closure or compatible function callable. A callback’s own parameter and return declarations still matter; callable alone does not encode a full generic function signature.

doubleValue(...) creates a Closure referring to the function without calling it. The literal ... in this position is first-class callable syntax, not argument unpacking. apply later invokes it with 4 and checks its own int return declaration.
Expected output or behavior: 8. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Separate the moment a callable is created from the moment apply invokes it. You may trace it without a PHP interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

lessons.title: Attributes as explicit metadata
lessons.summary: If Topic is annotated #[Label("practice")], what prints?
explanation: #[...] attaches attribute metadata to a declaration. #[Attribute(Attribute::TARGET_CLASS)] marks Label as a class-targeted attribute type. Label("study") records an argument; it does not automatically change how Topic behaves.

ReflectionClass inspects a known class declaration. Topic::class supplies its class-name string. getAttributes returns attribute descriptors; newInstance constructs the selected attribute object and runs its constructor. Inspect only metadata you intend to trust; construction can execute code.
Expected output or behavior: study. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain the difference between obtaining an attribute descriptor and constructing its object. You may trace it without a PHP interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

lessons.title: Reflection and declared structure
lessons.summary: If run is declared private instead, what prints?
explanation: ReflectionClass and ReflectionMethod expose declared structure. getMethod("run") finds the named method, and isPublic reports its visibility. This does not invoke run or prove that calling it with arbitrary input is safe.

Reflection is useful for tools and explicit metadata frameworks, not a reason to expose arbitrary method names from an untrusted request. The example examines a known local class and prints one Boolean label only.
Expected output or behavior: public. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
